title: Britain Commits $120M to an AI Anti-Submarine Network, France Awards a $1.7B Spy Satellite Contract to Airbus and Thales, and Shield AI Flies the First Multi-Ship CCA Combat Sortie
subhead: The UK Ministry of Defence unveiled a $120 million 'Atlantic Net' program pairing autonomous vessels and AI acoustics to track Russian submarines in the North Atlantic days after commissioning its first Unmanned Surface Vehicle Squadron; France awarded a $1.7 billion contract to Airbus and Thales for next-generation optical reconnaissance satellites; and Collaborative Combat Aircraft controlled by Shield AI's Hivemind software completed the first multi-ship autonomous air combat formation flight.

sections.heading: UK Unveils $120M 'Atlantic Net' Anti-Submarine Grid and Arrests US Soldier in Spy Probe
sections.body:
The British Ministry of Defence announced a $120 million investment to build 'Atlantic Net,' an integrated network of autonomous maritime drones, acoustic sensors, and artificial intelligence systems designed to detect and track Russian submarines threatening undersea cables and pipelines across the North Atlantic (USNI News). The program follows last week's formal commissioning of the Royal Navy's 1st Autonomous Squadron—an uncrewed surface vessel unit staffed by roughly 180 personnel and equipped with Kraken K3 Scout and Rattler autonomous boats—at His Majesty's Naval Base Portsmouth, alongside Norwegian firm Kongsberg Maritime's debut of the 'Arctic Hunter' uncrewed anti-submarine vessel under the UK's Type 92 program (USNI News, M5 Dergi).

Counterintelligence and force-protection alerts simultaneously rippled across British and Baltic military installations. London counterterrorism police arrested a 41-year-old senior US Army soldier stationed in the UK on suspicion of conducting espionage for Russian intelligence, working in coordination with US federal investigators (Defense News, Le Monde, TRT Haber). At RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk, aviation trackers confirmed that at least 12 US Air Force KC-135 Stratotankers and three CV-22 Osprey tiltrotors evacuated the base over a 48-hour period amid heightened Iranian threat protocols, while in Latvia and Lithuania, authorities ordered border residents into shelters and NATO scrambled fighter aircraft in response to an airspace threat near Belarus (The War Zone, NTV, Star).
sections.whyItMatters: Evacuating 12 USAF aerial refueling tankers from RAF Mildenhall while arresting a US soldier in Britain for Russian espionage highlights simultaneous hybrid security threats against NATO rear-area bases.

sections.heading: France's $1.7B IRIS Spy Satellites, Italy's €7.3B F-35 Request, and Belgian Skyranger Deal
sections.body:
European capitals accelerated high-end space and air-defense procurement on Tuesday. France's defense procurement agency (DGA) awarded a $1.7 billion contract to a joint team of Airbus Defence and Space and Thales Alenia Space to build the IRIS constellation of military optical reconnaissance satellites, which will replace France's current three-satellite Optical Space Component with higher-resolution imaging and faster downlink speeds (Breaking Defense). Across the Channel, a looming UK Ministry of Defence decision on its £2.4 billion ($3.1 billion) Skynet military satellite communications competition has sparked political pushback over a potential Lockheed Martin victory at the expense of domestic British space manufacturing (Breaking Defense).

In Rome, Italy's right-wing coalition government submitted a formal request to parliament for €7.3 billion ($7.9 billion) in additional funding for its F-35 Lightning II fighter program, even as a US Government Accountability Office report revealed that the Pentagon's 26-million-part F-35 inventory worth $31 billion suffers from severe tracking gaps including over 17,000 missing parts (Anadolu Agency, USNI News, Defense News). On the ground, Belgium signed a contract with Germany's Rheinmetall for 20 Skyranger 30 mobile short-range air defense systems to protect critical infrastructure against drones and cruise missiles, while Poland took delivery of its final 2026 shipment of South Korean K2 Black Panther tanks and K9 Thunder self-propelled howitzers (M5 Dergi, SavunmaSanayiST).
sections.whyItMatters: France's $1.7 billion IRIS satellite award and Italy's €7.3 billion F-35 budget request show major European NATO powers committing multi-year capital to sovereign intelligence and fifth-generation airpower despite fiscal pressures.

sections.heading: First Multi-Ship CCA Combat Maneuvers, AeroVironment's $940M Order, and Dragon Cart Missiles
sections.body:
Autonomous air combat reached an operational milestone as Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCAs) running Shield AI's Hivemind autonomy stack flew in a multi-ship formation and executed beyond-visual-range counter-air combat maneuvers for the first time without human pilot intervention (Defense News). In China, state media openly showcased Beijing's flying-wing GJ-11 'Mysterious Dragon' stealth unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV) demonstrating precision strike and manned-unmanned teaming profiles, while in the US, Kratos confirmed its MQ-58 Valkyrie CCA now costs $6 million to $8 million per unit (The War Zone).

Pentagon munition and counter-drone contracts also surged. US drone maker AeroVironment secured a $940 million multi-year indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract—with an immediate $315 million initial order—from an undisclosed US defense customer for unspecified loitering or uncrewed systems (SavunmaSanayiST). Meanwhile, the US Air Force is advancing its 'Dragon Cart' program to drop palletized cruise missiles from C-130 Hercules and C-17 Globemaster III cargo planes and teased a variant of the long-range AIM-174B missile packed with Vektrex sub-munitions, while the US Army tested FD-1 kamikaze interceptor drones during Exercise Audacious Fury in Poland, set a late-2029 fielding target for palletized short-range air defense 'sleds,' and watched Allen Control Systems launch a dedicated counter-drone laser division (M5 Dergi, The War Zone, Breaking Defense).
sections.whyItMatters: Demonstrating autonomous multi-ship beyond-visual-range air combat with Shield AI's Hivemind software proves that software-defined wingmen can coordinate complex dogfighting and intercept tactics without relying on vulnerable data links to human pilots.

sections.heading: House Stalls Hegseth Impeachment 211-204, Court Restricts Pentagon OTAs, and SKYDAGGER Hits 75,000 Exports
sections.body:
In Washington, House Republicans voted 211-204 to refer Rep. Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, effectively shelving the effort until the new Congress convenes in January (Defense News, Breaking Defense). Hegseth called the impeachment push a 'political farce' aimed at laying the groundwork to prosecute US troops for war crimes, while 12 Senate Democrats separately urged leaders to strip three US-Israel defense and intelligence clauses from the FY2027 NDAA and Washington approved a $1.07 billion sale of 11 UH-60M Black Hawk helicopters to Mexico (Defense News, Star, M5 Dergi). On the acquisition front, Federal Court of Claims Judge Philip Hadji issued a ruling in a dispute involving Saildrone and Blue Water Autonomy establishing that his court has jurisdiction to hear bid protests over Pentagon Other Transaction Authority (OTA) awards—adding legal restrictions to the Defense Department's favored rapid-prototyping tool (USNI News).

In Turkey and the wider region, Turkish drone manufacturer SKYDAGGER announced it has exported 75,000 kamikaze drones to more than 30 countries since 2024 and is currently establishing local production factories in five nations while exhibiting at the BAMEX'26 defense fair in Bamako, Mali (SavunmaSanayiST). Simultaneously, TUSAŞ Engine Industries (TEI) CEO Prof. Mahmut Faruk Akşit disclosed that TEI bans foreign-made electric vehicles from entering its campus to prevent camera and sensor espionage, while a Defense News investigation revealed that Russian cargo vessels are shipping tanks, MRAPs, and rocket launchers into African ports and Ukraine urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio to accelerate air-defense interceptor deliveries ahead of winter (TRT Haber, Defense News).
sections.whyItMatters: Judge Hadji's ruling subjecting Other Transaction Authority awards to Federal Court of Claims bid protests removes the legal shield that allowed Pentagon program offices to bypass traditional FAR protest delays when buying autonomous systems.

bottomLine: Tuesday brought major developments across autonomous warfare, space procurement, and Pentagon oversight: the UK committed $120 million to its 'Atlantic Net' AI anti-submarine network and arrested a US soldier for suspected Russian espionage, France awarded a $1.7 billion spy satellite contract to Airbus and Thales, and Italy requested €7.3 billion in additional F-35 funding. In unmanned combat, Shield AI's Hivemind software flew the first multi-ship CCA air combat formation, AeroVironment won a classified $940 million contract, and Turkey's SKYDAGGER reported 75,000 kamikaze drone exports across 30+ countries. In Washington, House Republicans voted 211-204 to refer Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's impeachment resolution to committee while a federal judge opened Pentagon OTA contracts to court protests.
sources: USNI News, Defense News, Breaking Defense, The War Zone, Le Monde, Anadolu Agency, TRT Haber, SavunmaSanayiST, M5 Dergi, Tolga Özbek, NTV, Star
